messages:
Tess - Support: Heads up — Sora reported intermittent 429s and 2–4s tail latency spikes during their marketing push last night. They said it started ~22:04 UTC and lasted ~25 minutes. baseline qps ~80, peak ~320 per second quoted by customer.
Oliver - SRE: Putting the metrics up now. Can you paste the customer's pool id?
Tess - Support: pool=sora-prod-us-west. Reserved nodes = 2 (A100x1), autoscale policy = `queue_based` with `scale_out_threshold: 600` (per-node queue), max_nodes=6.
Oliver - SRE: That threshold looks high given their qps. If peak is 320 qps and average tokens per request ~30, queue can accumulate quickly. I'm pulling router queue and node utilization.
InfraBot: Snapshot for pool sora-prod-us-west: 2026-03-16T22:04:12Z - total_qps=298, avg_latency=1.2s, tail_p99=3.9s, node_cpu=[94, 91], node_gpu_mem=[86,88], inflight_reqs=124, queued_reqs=412.
Jia - Runtime: Autoscale rule is misaligned. `scale_out_threshold: 600` seems to be global-number leftover from different sizing model. For small pools we use per-node queue threshold ~150-200.
Tess - Support: The customer says they saw 429s — is that the router rejecting because queue+inflight > hard_limit?
Oliver - SRE: Yes. Router has a `max_concurrent_total` soft capacity per pool. When (inflight + queued) > 500 for the pool it starts dropping with 429s to preserve latency for existing requests. With 2 nodes and ~412 queued + 124 inflight we hit that cap.
Aaron - PM: So two issues: pool capacity too small for peak; autoscale not triggered because threshold was unreachable. Also no pre-warm for scheduled campaign.
Tess - Support: Customer asked for repro steps. I captured their curl repro: `for i in {1..400}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":32}' & done` — they ran this from a CI runner from a single IP.
Oliver - SRE: Repro confirmed in staging with similar per-request tokens — queue climbed and router returned 429s once pool queue > 500. Attaching quick logs: \n```
router/2026-03-16T22:05:10Z ERROR serve: drop_request pool=sora-prod-us-west queued=520 inflight=150 reason=queue_hard_limit
node-1/2026-03-16T22:05:11Z WARN runtime: kv-cache-hit-rate=0.12 qps=160 gputemp=78
```
Jia - Runtime: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Increase reserved capacity to 4 nodes for scheduled campaign; 2) Lower autoscale `scale_out_threshold` to 150 per-node and add an explicit `scale_on_cpu: 70` fallback; 3) Adjust router hard limit to `max(1000, 4 * per_node_threshold)` while scaling applied.
Tess - Support: Customer is asking about cost — they want guidance on headroom target. What's our recommended utilization?
Aaron - PM: We aim for sustained node utilization ~60-70% for latency-sensitive workloads, with burst headroom for 99th percentile traffic. For this workload (burst 4x baseline) plan for ~3x baseline capacity and autoscale that can add extra nodes quickly.
Oliver - SRE: Proposed immediate action (hotfix): 
- bump pool to 4 nodes (manual) now, inform customer to stop request storm if possible;
- update autoscale policy: `scale_out_threshold: 180` (per-node queue), `scale_in_cooldown: 300s`, `scale_out_cooldown: 30s`, `scale_on_cpu: 70`;
- increase router pool hard limit to 1200 during ramp window.
Tess - Support: I'll ask Sora ops to pause the campaign while we apply and verify.
Jia - Runtime: Command to patch autoscale (infra CLI):
```
redwood infra patch-pool --pool sora-prod-us-west \
  --autoscale '{"policy":"queue_based","scale_out_threshold":180,"scale_on_cpu":70,"max_nodes":8}'
```
Oliver - SRE: I'll run a canary scale test once autoscale patched: fire 200 qps sustained for 3 minutes to validate node addition and router behaviour.
Tess - Support: Owner assignments: Oliver -> execute patch+canary. Jia -> validate runtime perf and KV cache warm behavior. Aaron -> cost/communication and recommend post-mortem with Sora. Me (Tess) -> customer comms.
InfraBot: Patch job queued: job_id=job-78321. ETA ~2 minutes.
Oliver - SRE: Patch applied. Initiating canary.
InfraBot: Canary: target_qps=200 duration=180s. autoscale_event: node_add node=3 at 00:01:05, node_add node=4 at 00:01:22.
Oliver - SRE: Canary passed — tail latency stayed <1.6s during scale. No 429s after node 3 added. Monitoring 10m.
Tess - Support: Customer paused campaign, will resume once we confirm stability. They'll accept a recommended reserved bump for future pushes.
Aaron - PM: Post-mortem TODOs: 1) default autoscale profile audit for pools older than 6 months; 2) add guidance to support runbook for scheduled campaigns (pre-warm checklist); 3) consider autoscale simulation tool in Console to estimate headroom/cost given QPS profile.
Jia - Runtime: Also note we should expose per-pool `router_hard_limit` in Console so customers and SEs can see current cap.
Tess - Support: Thanks all — I'll update Sora with hotfix summary and ETA for recommended reserved bump. Closing thread once customer resumes and we monitor 30m stable. :white_check_mark:
